discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Applied Materials, Israel (formerly University of Texas at Austin)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: moiré quantum materials and strongly correlated two-dimensional electron systems
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees makes the electronic bands nearly flat, so that electron interactions should dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers built such devices and found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be switched on with a gate. Together these works created twistronics: a controllable way to design strongly correlated and topological quantum matter by stacking and twisting atomically thin layers. Laboratories around the world have reproduced and extended the results. Scanning-probe, transport and optical experiments have revealed correlated Chern insulators, nematicity, Wigner crystals and, in moiré systems, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect. Few discoveries in condensed matter since the high-temperature superconductors have opened so large a field, and this one grew from a clean theoretical prediction confirmed by a decisive experiment.
